extracted.intended_audience: BBC journalists, editors, producers and other BBC content staff
extracted.subtask_description: Organization-wide editorial guidelines for BBC TV, radio and online content setting values, standards and topic-specific rules for producing and reviewing output. Covers accuracy, impartiality, privacy, children, advertising, audience interaction and mandatory referral/approval processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Guidelines (core statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Editorial Guidelines are the BBC's values and standards. They apply to all our content, wherever and however it is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets organisation-wide principles that govern all BBC output; acts as the primary standard against which content is judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Policy Guidance Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Policy Guidance Notes supplement the Editorial Guidelines, with further explanation of their themes and practical tips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides additional explanatory material and practical tips to interpret and apply the core guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Election Guidelines (including specific by-election guidance and related rules)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules and guidance to be followed during election periods to ensure fairness, impartiality and compliance with broadcasting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and Portrayal of Tribal Peoples
rubrics_metrics.description: New Guidance on the Reporting and Portrayal of Tribal Peoples
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic-specific guidance on sensitive and accurate reporting of tribal peoples and related communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for BBC Global News on Marketing Events
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for BBC Global News on Marketing Events launched
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules and guidance governing BBC Global News involvement in marketing events to protect editorial integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Modules (editorial topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training modules available on crime, polls and surveys, partnerships and competitions, plus modules explaining Accuracy, Impartiality, Strong Language, Violence, Secret Recording, Consent, Children and other issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory/encouraged training to help staff understand and apply Editorial Guidelines across specific topical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Integrity and Independence for Commercial Services
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Guidelines for BBC Commercial Services on Editorial Integrity and Independence from External Interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules that commercial arms of the BBC must follow to maintain editorial independence from commercial/advertising interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and Sponsorship Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: BBC Worldwide Advertising and Sponsorship Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards governing advertising, sponsorship and branded content to protect the BBC brand and editorial standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 1: The BBC's Editorial Values
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1: The BBC's Editorial Values / Editorial Values
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the fundamental editorial values (e.g. accuracy, impartiality, independence, fairness) that underpin all content decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 2: Using the Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 2: Using the Guidelines — Other Sources of Advice; Roles and Responsibilities; Principles and Practices; Editorial Justification; Guidance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how staff should use the Guidelines, where to seek advice, responsibilities for editorial decisions, and how to record editorial justification for risky or novel content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3: Accuracy — Principles; Finding contributors; Mandatory Referrals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for verifying facts, sourcing contributors, correcting errors and when to escalate issues for referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 5: Harm and Offence
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5: Harm and Offence — includes topics such as Imitative Behaviour and Alcohol, Smoking, Solvent Abuse and Illegal Drugs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on avoiding and minimising harm and offence, including handling of content that could encourage dangerous imitation or normalise substance misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 6: Fairness, Contributors and Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6: Fairness, Contributors and Consent — Contributors, Access Agreements and Editorial Independence; Anonymity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles for fair treatment of contributors, obtaining informed consent, managing access agreements and protecting editorial independence from contributors' influence; rules on granting anonymity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 7: Privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 7: Privacy — Doorstepping; Secret Recording; Principles; Mandatory Referrals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules protecting individuals' privacy, limits on intrusive reporting techniques (e.g. doorstepping, secret recording) and circumstances requiring referral or approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 9: Children and Young People as Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 9: Children and Young People as Contributors — includes Interacting with Children and Young People Online (Parts 1 & 2); Informed Consent guidance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards and safeguards for working with minors, assessing risk, obtaining consent and online child-safety measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interacting with Children and Young People Online (guidance in full)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance in Full — Working with Children and Young People; Who Gives Informed Consent?; How we Obtain Informed Consent; What is Informed Consent?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedures for consent, risk assessment and protecting child contributors in online and broadcast contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 12: Religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 12: Religion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on reporting religious beliefs and communities sensitively and accurately to avoid offence and ensure balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 13: Re-Use and Reversioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 13: Re-Use and Reversioning — Principles; Mandatory Referrals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for re-using or re-versioning existing content, including copyright, rights clearances and when to escalate decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 14: Editorial Integrity and Independence from External Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 14: Editorial Integrity and Independence from External Interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules to prevent external interests (commercial, political or other) from influencing editorial content and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 16: External Relationships and Funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 16: External Relationships and Funding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on managing relationships with external organisations, sponsorship, funding and associated transparency or referral requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 17: Interacting with our Audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 17: Interacting with our Audiences — Phone-in Programmes, User Generated Content Online, Mobile Content, Games and Interactive TV; Talent Shows; Game Shows and Quizzes; Telephone Services; Prizes; Pre-recorded or Repeated Programmes; Awards; Voting; Competitions; Principles; Mandatory Referrals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for audience-facing formats and interactive features, covering fairness, transparency, permissions, competition rules, prizes and moderation/escallation processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 19: Accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 19: Accountability — Principles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements for accountability, handling complaints, corrections and internal/external oversight mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Referrals (escalation requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory Referrals (listed across multiple sections)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many topics include mandatory referral rules: specific situations must be escalated to editorial policy or senior management for approval before broadcast/publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Links / External Regulatory Frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Related Links: Commissioning at the BBC; BBC Complaints; BBC Trust; Ofcom Broadcasting Code; Defence Advisory Notice Committee
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance requires compliance with external regulators (Ofcom), internal governance bodies and reference to complaints and commissioning processes.
